practiceQuestions.q: What is the core foundational concept of the Gandhian economic strategy focusing on village self-reliance?
opts: Industrial Capitalism
Gram Swaraj
State Socialism
Global Mercantilism
practiceQuestions.sol: Gram Swaraj refers to the Gandhian ideal of village self-reliance where every village is self-sustained and capable of managing its own affairs, forming the bedrock of Gandhian economic strategy. [Primary Reference: NCERT History & Gandhian Economic Thought]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following institutions was established by Mahatma Gandhi to promote Khadi and village industries?
opts: All India Spinners' Association
Planning Commission
National Development Council
FICCI
practiceQuestions.sol: Mahatma Gandhi established the All India Spinners' Association (Charkha Sangh) in 1923 to propagate Khadi and revive rural cottage industries. [Primary Reference: Standard Historical Canons - Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: In the Gandhian economic framework, what does the doctrine of 'Trusteeship' propose?
opts: Total nationalization of all private property by the state
Wealthy people holding their wealth as trustees for the welfare of society
Unregulated accumulation of capital through free-market mechanisms
Abolition of all forms of labor and industrial production
practiceQuestions.sol: Trusteeship provides a means by which the wealthy owners of wealth would be trustees of their surplus wealth for the benefit of society, avoiding violent revolution. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Economic Philosophy / Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi]

practiceQuestions.q: Which concept best describes Gandhi's view on mechanization and machinery?
opts: Unrestricted embrace of heavy industrialization
Absolute rejection of all tools and metal implements
Opposition to machinery that displaces human labor and creates unemployment
Prioritizing automation over human welfare universally
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi did not oppose machines per se; he opposed the 'craze' for machinery that saves labor when that labor is sitting idle and starving, advocating instead for tools that enhance human efficiency without causing unemployment. [Primary Reference: Hind Swaraj / Gandhian Economic Thought]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Khadi in the Gandhian economic strategy?
opts: A symbol of luxury and elite fashion
An instrument of economic self-reliance, rural employment, and swadeshi
A commercial product exclusively for foreign export
A tool for centralized factory production
practiceQuestions.sol: Khadi was the economic embodiment of Swadeshi, providing supplementary income to millions of impoverished farmers during lean agricultural seasons and fostering village self-sufficiency. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following principles forms the foundation of Gandhian critique of modern industrial civilization?
opts: Material hedonism and unending consumption
Simple living and voluntary limitation of wants
Aggressive urbanization and migration to mega-cities
Maximal exploitation of natural resources
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi argued that 'the earth provides enough to satisfy every man's needs, but not every man's greed,' making simple living and limitation of wants central to his thought. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Writings / Hind Swaraj]

practiceQuestions.q: The All India Village Industries Association (AIVIA) was founded in which year under Gandhi's guidance?
practiceQuestions.sol: AIVIA was established in 1934 with headquarters at Wardha to revive and promote rural and village industries other than Khadi. [Primary Reference: Economic History of India / Collected Works]

practiceQuestions.q: What does 'Bread Labour' (Sharir Shram) mean in Gandhian economics?
opts: Working only for monetary wages in multinational corporations
The moral obligation of every individual to perform physical labor to earn their livelihood
Exploitation of agricultural laborers by landlords
Importing food grains from foreign nations
practiceQuestions.sol: Derived from Russian writer T.M. Bondarev's concept, Gandhi's 'Bread Labour' posits that every person must perform physical labor to earn their daily bread, fostering social equality and dignity of labor. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Ethical Framework]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution specifically reflects Gandhian economic ideology regarding village panchayats?
opts: Article 39
Article 40
Article 44
Article 48A
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 40 directs the State to organize village panchayats and endow them with necessary powers to function as units of self-government, embodying Gandhian decentralized democracy. [Primary Reference: Article 40, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was Mahatma Gandhi's stance on centralization of economic power?
opts: It is essential for rapid economic growth
It leads to the exploitation of masses and must be avoided through decentralization
It should be managed exclusively by private monopolies
It has no bearing on social justice
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi believed that centralization is inherently violent and incompatible with a non-violent, egalitarian society, advocating instead for decentralized production units. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Economic Thought]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Gandhian economic strategy fundamentally contrast with the Nehruvian model of development?
opts: Gandhi prioritized heavy industries, whereas Nehru prioritized cottage industries
Gandhi focused on decentralized village self-sufficiency, whereas Nehru emphasized heavy industrialization and state-led planning
Both models completely rejected modern science and technology
Gandhi advocated corporate capitalism while Nehru advocated feudalism
practiceQuestions.sol: While the Gandhian model centers on Gram Swaraj, cottage industries, and moral restraint, the Nehruvian model focused on heavy capital-goods industries, scientific temper, and centralized public sector planning for rapid modernization. [Primary Reference: Economic History of Independent India]

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of trusteeship, how does Gandhi propose to handle capitalists who refuse to act as trustees?
opts: Immediate armed insurrection and physical liquidation
Non-violent non-cooperation and peaceful satyagraha by workers
Unconditional state bailout and tax exemptions
Complete surrender of labor rights to corporate boards
practiceQuestions.sol: If capitalists refuse trusteeship, Gandhi advocated non-violent non-cooperation and Satyagraha by workers, believing that capital cannot survive without the willing cooperation of labor. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Socialism & Trusteeship Doctrine]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Gandhi advocate for 'Production by the masses' rather than 'Mass production'?
opts: Mass production concentrates wealth and causes mass unemployment, whereas production by the masses ensures distributive justice and employment
Mass production is too slow and inefficient compared to handlooms
Production by the masses relies exclusively on imported foreign machinery
Mass production guarantees ecological sustainability
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi famously critiqued mass production because it concentrates power and goods in few hands and displaces millions of workers, whereas production by the masses utilizes decentralized human energy for universal employment. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Economic Critique]

practiceQuestions.q: How does Gandhian economic strategy address the environmental and ecological crisis?
opts: By promoting limitless industrial extraction of minerals
Through limitation of wants, sustainable local resource use, and harmony with nature
By encouraging heavy fossil-fuel combustion for high GDP growth
By relying solely on nuclear energy and mega-dams
practiceQuestions.sol: Long before modern environmentalism, Gandhian economics emphasized ethical restraint, low carbon footprint through local production, and reverence for nature, anticipating sustainable development. [Primary Reference: Ecological Thought of Mahatma Gandhi]

practiceQuestions.q: What role does the concept of 'Swadeshi' play in safeguarding domestic economies within Gandhian thought?
opts: Encouraging complete economic isolationism without any international trade
Using goods produced locally and supporting immediate neighbors to sustain village livelihoods
Mandating state monopolies over all retail trade
Promoting foreign direct investment in luxury goods
practiceQuestions.sol: Swadeshi is defined by Gandhi as that spirit in us which restricts us to the use and service of our immediate surroundings, promoting local self-reliance and protecting domestic artisans from ruinous foreign competition. [Primary Reference: Hind Swaraj / Gandhian Works]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Gandhi place utmost emphasis on agriculture and cattle breeding as part of the village economy?
opts: To generate massive agricultural exports for western markets
Because they form the natural twin pillars of sustenance, organic manure, and draught power for rural self-reliance
To facilitate corporate farming and land consolidation by multinational cartels
To replace all human labor with mechanized tractors
practiceQuestions.sol: Agriculture and cow protection/cattle breeding were viewed by Gandhi as inseparable from the village economy, providing food security, organic fertilizer, and animal power without dependence on fossil fuels. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Economic Agrarian Policy]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Gandhian model view the relationship between rights and duties in economic life?
opts: Rights are paramount, and duties are irrelevant
Real rights flow from a well-performed duty; performing duty automatically secures rights
Rights belong exclusively to the state, while duties belong to citizens
Neither rights nor duties have any place in economic planning
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi famously stated that all rights to be earned and preserved come from a duty well done. If we discharge our duties, rights will follow as a natural consequence. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Ethics & Philosophy]

practiceQuestions.q: What was Gandhi's view on taxation and state expenditure in an ideal decentralized economy?
opts: Heavy taxation to fund massive bureaucratic standing armies and luxury state infrastructure
Minimal taxation, with state expenditures focused on basic social welfare, education, and health of the poorest
Complete abolition of all forms of revenue collection and public administration
Regressive taxation penalizing cottage industries
practiceQuestions.sol: In a non-violent, decentralized society (Ramrajya), the state apparatus is minimal, and taxation is kept low, serving primarily as a trusteeship measure for upliftment of the most vulnerable (Antyodaya). [Primary Reference: Gandhian Political Economy]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Gandhian economic strategy conceptualize the division of labor?
opts: Rigid caste-based hereditary occupation hierarchy without mobility
Integration of mental and physical labor, where everyone engages in bread labor while respecting all forms of honest work
Extreme specialization leading to worker alienation
Abolition of all skilled labor in favor of unorganized manual scavenging
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi critiqued the hierarchical division of labor based on caste and alienation in modern factories, advocating instead for the dignity of all labor where intellectual and physical work are harmonized. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Social Thought]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the economic significance of 'Antyodaya' in the Gandhian framework?
opts: Prioritizing the economic growth of the wealthiest corporate houses first (Trickle-down)
The upliftment and welfare of the last, lowest, and most marginalized person in society
Focusing exclusively on urban industrial output metrics
Maximizing military expenditure at the cost of social sectors
practiceQuestions.sol: Antyodaya ('rise of the last') is the moral and economic benchmark of Gandhian strategy, stating that policy must be evaluated by how it benefits the poorest and most vulnerable person. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Economic Welfare Principles]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gandhian strategy of economic development:
1. It emphasizes heavy capital-intensive industrialization to achieve rapid GDP growth.
2. It places supreme importance on moral growth, human dignity, and the limitation of material wants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Gandhi strongly opposed heavy capital-intensive industrialization that caused unemployment and urbanization. Statement 2 is correct as Gandhian strategy centers on human dignity, moral growth, and limitation of wants. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Economic Philosophy]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Trusteeship concept in Gandhian thought:
1. It envisages the legal confiscation of all private property by the government.
2. It allows private owners to retain management of wealth but requires them to use it as a trust for society.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because trusteeship rejects violent confiscation or state nationalization; instead, it relies on moral transformation and voluntary surrender of surplus. Statement 2 is correct. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Trusteeship Framework]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Gram Swaraj':
1. It visualizes each village as a self-contained, self-governing republic producing its own food, clothing, and basic necessities.
2. It advocates complete autarky and total prohibition of all external trade with other regions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Gram Swaraj is built on village republics that are self-reliant in basic needs. Statement 2 is incorrect because Gandhi did not advocate rigid isolationism or total prohibition of trade; he envisioned interdependent concentric circles where villages trade surplus voluntarily without exploitation. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Village Republics]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the All India Spinners' Association and All India Village Industries Association:
1. Both organizations were founded under the direct guidance of Mahatma Gandhi to support rural economic revival.
2. They focused exclusively on exporting Indian handicrafts to British markets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct as both bodies were promoted by Gandhi for Khadi and village industries. Statement 2 is incorrect because their primary objective was domestic self-sufficiency and rural employment, not exporting to British markets. [Primary Reference: National Movement & Economic Institutions]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Bread Labour':
1. It implies that every person must engage in physical labor to earn their food.
2. It was a concept originally formulated by Gandhi without any external intellectual influence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; bread labour requires everyone to do physical work. Statement 2 is incorrect because Gandhi acknowledged that he borrowed the concept of bread labour from Russian writer T.M. Bondarev (and also influenced by John Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'). [Primary Reference: Gandhian Intellectual Influences]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the integration of Gandhian economic principles into the Constitution of India:
1. Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) contains provisions directly inspired by Gandhian ideology, such as promotion of cottage industries and organization of village panchayats.
2. Fundamental Rights in Part III explicitly mandate the trusteeship model of corporate governance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; articles like 40, 43 (promotion of cottage industries) embody Gandhian principles in DPSP. Statement 2 is incorrect because Fundamental Rights do not mention the trusteeship model; trusteeship remains an ethical-economic framework rather than a codified constitutional mandate in Part III. [Primary Reference: Constitution of India, Parts III & IV]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning Gandhi's critique of industrial capitalism:
1. Gandhi argued that industrial capitalism inherently fosters competition, class warfare, and spiritual degradation.
2. He proposed that labor unions should rely on violent strikes and sabotage to overthrow factory owners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Gandhi viewed industrial capitalism as morally corrosive. Statement 2 is incorrect because Gandhi strictly prohibited violence, sabotage, and coercive strikes, advocating instead for peaceful arbitration, constructive cooperation, and non-violent Satyagraha. [Primary Reference: Gandhian Labor Relations & Ethics]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the concept of decentralized economy in Gandhian thought:
1. Decentralization prevents economic power from being concentrated in the hands of a few state or corporate entities.
2. It requires complex multinational supply chains to distribute essential goods efficiently.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; decentralization is designed to prevent monopoly and concentration of economic power. Statement 2 is incorrect because Gandhian strategy explicitly rejects complex multinational supply chains in favor of local production and local consumption (Swadeshi). [Primary Reference: Gandhian Decentralized Planning]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding J.C. Kumarappa and Gandhian economics:
1. J.C. Kumarappa was a pioneering economist who systematically formulated Gandhian economic doctrines and philosophy.
2. He advocated for a 'permanent economy' that harmonizes human economic activity with the regenerative capacities of nature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. J.C. Kumarappa is widely regarded as the creator of Gandhian economic thought, publishing seminal works like 'Economy of Permanence' which integrated economics with ecology. [Primary Reference: J.C. Kumarappa & Gandhian Economic Literature]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of machinery in Gandhian economy:
1. Gandhi completely rejected the invention of the sewing machine and the printing press.
2. His opposition was directed at the 'fetishism' of machinery that enslaves humanity and creates mass unemployment rather than tools that ease manual burden.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Gandhi famously stated that he did not object to the Singer sewing machine; he recognized it as a useful tool for households. Statement 2 is correct, highlighting that his critique was against exploitative, labor-displacing machinery. [Primary Reference: Young India / Gandhian Writings on Machinery]
